title: Backlog storage shape
description: Canonical shape of a project's backlog, used by every radin agent/skill that reads or appends to it (radin-review, radin-record, radin-execute, radin-plan). This schema documents the contract in JSON form for radin contributors — it is not read at runtime; each agent/skill embeds the concrete shape matching this schema directly in its own instructions, since installed skills/agents run in consumer repos that never receive this docs/ directory. Storage is $NAMESPACE_DIR/backlog/index.jsonl (one 'indexLine' object per line, JSON Lines not a JSON array) plus one 'taskFile' per task under $NAMESPACE_DIR/backlog/tasks/, where an epic is a subdirectory holding DESCRIPTION.md (the shared root context) and its child tasks.

indexLine.description: One line of index.jsonl, one line per task, in no particular order (category grouping/order is a presentation concern `radin-backlog.sh show` applies at render time, not a storage concern).

id.description: Slug derived from the title when the task is created by `radin-backlog.sh add`, deduped with a numeric suffix on collision. Stable for the task's lifetime, even if the title is later edited — this is the key `depends_on` and radin-plan/radin-execute use, never the title.

category.description: Semver-style change type, same vocabulary as a conventional-commit type. There is no per-entry bracket tag on top of this.

title.description: Human-readable heading text, used for display and as a fallback lookup key (exact then case-insensitive substring) when a caller doesn't have the id.

priority.description: Human-set importance, higher is more important. Gaps and duplicates are allowed, so inserting a task never forces a renumber. The key is absent when unset, and absent must stay distinguishable from any number: "did a human decide this?" is the question a prioritization pass has to answer, so no verb defaults it. `radin-backlog.sh list` orders set priorities descending with unset entries after every set one.

depends_on.description: Human-authored ordering over other tasks' ids. Absent or empty means unset. `radin-backlog.sh set-deps` refuses an unknown id, a self-reference and a cycle, and `remove` prunes the removed id from every other entry's array — an unresolvable dependency stalls `radin state deps-check` rather than failing it.

file.description: Either "tasks/<id>.md" or "tasks/<epic-id>/<id>.md" for a task grouped under an epic, relative to the backlog/ directory. Points at the matching taskFile, and is the only carrier of epic membership: an epic itself gets no index line and no category. One nesting level only.

taskFile.description: Free-form markdown at $BACKLOG_TASKS_DIR/<id>.md: the task's description, as exhaustive as the situation warrants — what the change is, why it matters, affected files/areas if known, acceptance criteria if known. radin-execute/radin-plan derive scope and priority entirely from this text, so a thin one-liner starves them of what they need; write enough that a sub-agent picking up only this file (no other session context) could act on it correctly. May end with one or more '**Plan:** <path>' lines, appended by radin-plan after it plans this task (more than one means radin-plan judged the task's scope broad enough to split into independent sub-plans, and the user confirmed the split). Splitting each task into its own file means inserting a **Plan:** line here can never shift or otherwise affect any other task's file.
